title: Three more military UFO videos declassified by Trump admin
excerpt: "It’s time the American people see it for themselves," says Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
content:
The Trump administration on Friday released another three videos showing what it described as Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs), commonly known as UFOs.

This is the eighth release in a series that began with the first tranche of documents being published on May 8 following an instruction from President Trump.

The videos were published by the Department of Defense, which the administration calls the Department of War though Congress hasn’t formally approved the name change.

Read More on News

In an accompanying statement, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said: "The Department of War is in lockstep with President Trump to bring unprecedented transparency regarding our government’s understanding of unidentified anomalous phenomena. These files, hidden behind classifications, have long fueled justified speculation—and it’s time the American people see it for themselves.

"This release of declassified documents demonstrates the Trump administration’s earnest commitment to unprecedented transparency."

What The New Videos Show

The three newly released videos were all filmed in the Middle East in 2020, 2023 and 2026 respectively.

The oldest from 2020 is 20 seconds long and appears to have been recorded at or slightly above sea level. The outline of a ship, the silhouette of which clearly resembles an aircraft carrier, can be seen while a small object appears to fly past and then further up into the sky. Several areas of the screen are concealed by black rectangles.

In the 2023 video, which is 13 seconds long, a small object can be seen moving around from above while appearing to rapidly change direction several times.

The 2026 video is the longest at 54 seconds, and appears to show several small objects moving as a group and is also filmed from above.

...

In an accompanying note the Department of Defense said: "The materials archived here are unresolved cases, meaning the government is unable to make a definitive determination on the nature of the observed phenomena. This can occur for a variety of reasons, including a lack of sufficient data, and the Department of War (DOW) welcomes the application of private-sector analysis, information and experience.

"DOW will continue to conduct separate reporting on resolved UAP cases, as mandated by statue. Under this administration we will pursue the truth and share our findings with the American people."

President Trump’s Directive

In February President Trump instructed the Department of Defense and other government departments and federal agencies to compile and then release government files related to aliens and UFOs.

On his Truth Social website the president wrote: "Based on the tremendous interest shown, I will be directing the Secretary of War, and other relevant departments and agencies, to begin the process of identifying and releasing government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life, unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP), and unidentified flying objects (UFOs), and any and all other information connected to these highly complex, but extremely interesting and important, matters. God bless America!"

Other UFO File Releases

In October a separate batch of files released by the Department of Defense included drawings and witness reports of alleged sightings of unidentified beings, referred to as "Skinwalkers," in Utah in 2010.

The initial reports led to a Utah Task Force investigation and in March and April 2010 there were two Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies (BAASS) visits to the reported locations.

The sightings were reported at a ranch near Fort Duchesne in northeastern Utah. Skinwalkers are figures described in Navajo folklore that can transform into various animals.

In April Republican Representative Tim Burchett, who has long campaigned for more information about UFOs to be made public, said he’d been briefed on some "pretty wild" things but was confident the American people "can handle it."

Burchett has previously said he believes the U.S. government has engaged in a decades long cover-up to conceal its recovery of alien technology and potentially extraterrestrial beings, though these claims have been widely discredited.

Congressional Hearings

In 2023 the House Oversight Committee held hearings into UFOs with witnesses saying the federal government had been aware of alien activity since the 1930s.

However these claims were criticized by some scientists, with physicist Brian Cox commenting: "I watched a few clips and saw some people who seemed to believe stuff saying extraordinary things without presenting extraordinary evidence."
